subject: bauhausBird
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: songbird on a branch.
Style: Bauhaus primary-colour geometry.

spec.name: Bauhaus Songbird on a Branch
spec.description: A small perched songbird built as a Bauhaus composition of circles, triangles and squares in flat red, yellow and blue, gripping a black branch that rests on a white plinth with two posts.
spec.layout: Real songbird scale: about 15 cm from beak tip to tail tip, standing about 16 cm above the floor (beak side +Z). Everything is centred on x = 0, the bird sits in the middle of a horizontal branch that runs along X, and the branch is held on two thin posts over a flat plinth lying on y = 0, so the plinth is the only thing touching the floor. The bird is seen in profile or three-quarter view and is a stack of simple solids, each a different primary shape. The body is a squat red ellipsoid (radii about 0.052 x, 0.05 y, 0.068 z) centred at [0, 0.17, 0]. Its head is a yellow sphere of radius 0.034 at [0, 0.228, 0.052], pushed forward and up. A blue pyramid or cone beak points forward from the head, with a smaller dark-blue lower beak on the jaw. The two blue wings lie folded against the flanks, slightly apart from the body and angled back and down, built as layered rectangular feathers. A fan of five rectangular tail feathers (yellow and blue) points back and slightly down to z = -0.19. Two thin yellow-dark legs come out of the belly and end in four-toed feet whose toes wrap over the branch top at y = 0.102. The style on every part is Bauhaus: bold geometry, flat primary colours (red, yellow and blue, plus black and off-white), no gradients, no organic detail. Circles are thin discs, squares are boxes, triangles are cones with 3 sides or extruded triangles. Each detail is a small separate part in its own flat colour, seated on the surface: eyes are stacked concentric discs (black outline, white, black pupil), bands are thin rings or boxes, and a black thin outline disc sits behind each coloured disc (about 0.0015 m larger) so shapes read as printed. Use low segment counts (8 to 12 around, 6 to 8 up) so facets show. Keep symmetric left/right pairs exact mirrors. Only the perch is on the floor. The bird's body, head, wings, tail and legs all sit above y = 0.10.

parts.builds: The whole head and neck collar. A yellow sphere head, radius 0.034, centred at headCenter, slightly flattened in y. A blue half-disc crest, an extruded semicircle about 0.028 wide, stands on the crown with a thin black outline disc behind it and a small red circle at its middle. On each side is a red cheek disc, radius 0.012, with a black outline disc behind it. The eyes sit on the front-sides of the head at about x ±0.022, y 0.235, z 0.075, each made of stacked discs: a black outline disc r 0.0125, a white disc r 0.0105, a black pupil disc r 0.006 and a tiny white highlight disc. A thin black brow bar sits above each eye, slanted slightly. The upper beak is a blue 4-sided pyramid or cone about 0.032 long, base radius 0.014, from beakBase pointing +Z, on the head bone. The lower beak is a smaller blueDark wedge on the jaw joint, with a thin black mouth-line box between them and two black nostril dots. Under the head is a neck collar: a white flat ring (short wide cylinder) with thin black rings above and below it, and a small red triangle bib point on the throat. Yellow-dark triangular feather points sit on the back of the head as a nape detail. Seat every detail on the sphere surface with stick.
parts.attaches: Neck collar sits on the top of the torso near neckBase. Head parts ride neck and head, and the lower beak rides jaw (hinge at jawHinge). Nothing in front of the face.

parts.builds: Body mass only, with the rump and the front of the chest. A red ellipsoid body (radii ~0.052, 0.05, 0.068) at bodyCenter, built as a loft or scaled sphere with 10 to 12 sides. An off-white belly half-ellipsoid or half-disc sits on the underside and front, hugging the body surface. A yellow chest bib triangle (extruded, pointing down, ~0.04 wide) sits on the front of the chest, outlined by a slightly larger black triangle behind it. Three thin black ring bands cross the breast, below the bib. A blueDark back saddle of overlapping rectangles lies along the top of the back. A yellow square rump patch is above the tail root. Thin black dividing bars separate the colour blocks. Two blue shoulder discs (r 0.014, black outline behind) sit on the flanks at the shoulderL and shoulderR mounts, but under the wings. Small red thigh-cover bumps (half spheres) sit at the hipSockets. All details are seated on the body surface using b.surface and stick.
parts.attaches: Head part's collar overlaps the top-front at neckBase. Wings start at shoulderL/R on the sides. Tail starts at tailRoot at the back. Legs come out below at hipSocketL/R.

parts.builds: Both wings and the tail, mirrored exactly. Each wing is a folded slab group that lies along the flank starting at the shoulder mount and angling back and slightly down and out (wingL1/2/3 and wingR1/2/3 bones). It has a blue covert panel (rounded/pointed extruded rectangle) over the shoulder, then 5 overlapping long primary feathers: rectangles with pointed ends in alternating blue and blueDark, longer toward the back, a yellow stripe bar across the middle, a red circle on the covert (with a black outline disc behind), and a white small square tip on each primary. A thin black edge line follows the leading edge. The tail is a fan of 5 rectangular feathers (thin boxes), 0.02 wide and 0.11 to 0.13 long, starting at tailRoot, running back and slightly down to z -0.19, spread by about 8 degrees each. The colours alternate yellow and blue, with the middle feather yellow, and each has a black end band and a white tip square. A red circle sits on the tail base, with a black outline behind it. Feathers on tail1/tail2/tail3 and wing bones by span.
parts.attaches: Wings start at the shoulderL/R mounts on the torso's flanks and sit just outside the body (x about ±0.052 to ±0.066). The tail starts at tailRoot, at the torso's back.

parts.builds: Both legs and feet, mirrored. Each has a short blueDark feather-trouser prism (small triangular or box block) at the hip socket. Under it, a thin yellowDark tarsus rod (radius ~0.0035) runs from hipSocket down to the foot, with a small red disc at the ankle and a black thin ring at the knee. Each foot has four toes: three forward and one back (toeX1..4 bones), thin yellowDark rods (radius ~0.003) that curl over and wrap the branch top at y 0.102 (toes end slightly below the branch's top silhouette edge, at about y 0.098 on the sides), each tipped with a black cone claw. The toes' pads are tiny black cubes. Feet sit exactly on branchTop at footL/footR.
parts.attaches: Hips at hipSocketL/R on the torso's underside. Toes grip the top of the branch at footL/footR (branch radius 0.012, axis y 0.09).

parts.builds: The branch and its stand, in a Bauhaus style. An off-white flat plinth box (0.34 long in x, 0.016 tall, 0.09 deep in z) lies on y = 0, with three small squares on its top face in red, yellow and blue and thin black edge lines. Two thin black posts (0.012 square, y 0.016 to 0.09) stand at postL and postR (x ±0.12). The branch is a dark (branch colour) faceted rod, radius 0.012 with 6 to 8 sides, along X at y 0.09 from x -0.17 to 0.17, with slightly tapered ends. It has rounded or flat end caps (a red disc at the left end, a blue disc at the right end), and thin yellow ring bands at x ±0.06 and ±0.15 and a few raised knots (branchLight small blocks). A twig rises from twigRoot (x 0.1) diagonally up and forward to about [0.15, 0.19, 0.03] as a thin sweep, with a short fork. Geometric leaves sit on the twig: a red circle disc, a yellow triangle and a blue square, each with a thin black outline shape behind it, each about 0.03 wide. They face +Z or the viewer. A matching small twig stub on the left end carries one yellow disc. No part of the perch intrudes into the area x within ±0.07 above y 0.102, which is the bird's space.
parts.attaches: Branch top at branchTop is where the bird's toes grip. All the perch's geometry rides the perch root joint. Its plinth is the only thing on y = 0.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out the spec for a songbird perched on a branch, in a Bauhaus primary-colour geometric style. I'm estimating the bird at about 15 cm long with a branch around 30 cm, and I'm sketching a rough bounding size while I decide the branch's orientation.

I'm settling the branch's placement now: it runs along X with the bird facing +Z, and the bird's feet grip the top of it. I'm still weighing whether the branch should rest on the floor or be held up by a small base, leaning toward a simple Bauhaus-style support.

I'm laying out the dimensions and placing the parts: the branch is about 0.34 m long, the bird sits centred on it, and I'm positioning the body, head, beak and tail by their coordinates, with the tail trailing back along -Z.

I'm checking the overall bounds now: the tail reaches back to about -0.17 on Z and the beak forward to about +0.10, so the box runs from roughly -0.18 to +0.10 on that axis. The branch sits centred on X, and I'm joining the rig's body, spine and hip joints along the bird's length.

I'm now setting out the rig's joints: the hips and chest run along the spine, with the neck, head and jaw above them, and the tail chain trailing back from the hips.

I'm settling the wings now, folded against the body with a slight outward angle, and placing their shoulder, elbow and wrist joints down the side.

I'm now placing the leg joints: the hip, knee and ankle for each leg sit down the body, with the toes at the front and hind toe gripping the branch. I'm keeping the legs short, with the body raised slightly so the feet clear the branch top.

I'm now working out how the rig's root joint and the branch's parts attach, since a static perch still needs a joint to carry it. I'm weighing whether to hang the branch off the hips or give it its own root at the base, and I'm leaning towards a separate root so that moving the bird doesn't drag the perch with it.

I'm splitting the work into parts: the torso will cover the body sphere, belly, back, breast stripes and rump, with the tail as its own piece, while the head will take the head sphere, beak, eyes, crown, cheek and neck collar.

I'm now splitting the budget across five parts: the head, torso, wings and tail, legs and feet, and the perch, with about 810 units in total. For the palette I'm using Bauhaus primaries, red, yellow and blue.

I'm now listing the colour palette: Bauhaus primaries red, yellow and blue, each with a darker and lighter shade, plus black and an off-white for contrast.

I'm weighing the colour scheme now, mapping the Bauhaus primaries onto the bird's parts: a blue head, a yellow beak, and a red body, with the wings in blue to contrast the red.

I'm now settling the colour mapping for the parts: yellow head, blue beak, red body, with the tail in dark blue and a yellow stripe, and a white belly half-disc and black legs. I'm setting the eyes as black with a white ring and a red cheek disc, then I'm placing the mount points for the branch top, both feet, the hip socket and the neck base.

Now I'm sizing the torso and head against each other, with the tail reaching back and the beak pushing forward to set the overall length.

I'm setting up the perch as a base plinth with two posts, then the branch rod on top, with terminal circles at each end and a twig angled up on the right with a leaf.

I'm sizing the wing and tail boxes now: the wings sit against the body's side at about x 0.052, and the tail runs back from z -0.06 to -0.19, sitting a little low so it clears the perch.

I'm sizing the legs and feet so the toes wrap over the branch top, then checking the head and torso boxes against the rig's neck and hip joints.

I'm now setting up the joint list for the rig, starting with the perch root at the origin pointing up, and I'm working out how the hips attach to it.

I'm defining the joint list for the rig: the tail chain starts at the hips and trails back along -Z, with its first joint pointing slightly downward.

Still defining the joint list for the wings and legs...

Still working through the rig's joint list: the toes on each foot take their own joints at the ankle, angled forward and back to grip the branch.

I'm now writing out the spec's style guidance, with Bauhaus geometry built from circles, triangles, squares and rectangles, and flat primary colours outlined in black. For the head, I'm placing a yellow sphere with a blue semicircle crest on top, red cheek discs on each side, and black eyes built from stacked discs.

I'm now detailing the head's finishing touches: black eyes with white rings and yellow highlights, brows, a blue two-part beak, black nostrils, and a white collar at the neck. Then I'm moving on to the torso, with a red body, a white underbelly, a dark-blue back plate, a yellow breast bib, and black chest stripes.

Still describing the wings and tail feathers, then moving on to the legs and feet.

Now I'm laying out the perch: a white plinth with black posts, a branch rod at about 0.09 with end caps and yellow bands, and a twig with leaves rising off to one side.

I'm checking the perch's dimensions now: a box about 0.34 m wide, 0.215 m tall and 0.095 m deep. The tallest point of the model is the head at about 0.265, so the overall height comes out near 0.27, and I'm confirming the budget totals roughly 810 units out of 900.
